title: What can fal.ai do for topics, images, content and moderation, at what cost, and where must the key never go?
summary: fal.ai models, pricing, queue API, webhooks, the MCP; storing generated assets in R2; moderation APIs (Workers AI Llama Guard, OpenAI moderation); Claude for content assistance; server-side-only key handling. AI is secondary to core infrastructure.

title: fal.ai flagship image model: FLUX.2 pro, $0.03 for first megapixel + $0.015 per extra
summary: A 1024x1024 (1MP) image costs $0.03; a 1920x1080 (2MP) image costs $0.045. Rounds up to the nearest megapixel. Confirmed by direct fetch of the model page, cross-checked against the pricing sentence twice (rendered + raw HTML). Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai budget image model: FLUX.1 schnell, $0.003 per megapixel, commercial rights included
summary: A 1024x1024 image rounds to 1MP = $0.003 -- 10x cheaper than the flagship pro model. The model page itself states commercial usage rights are included. Confirmed via raw HTML fetch of the model page. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai queue API: submit returns a request_id, three states, webhook or poll
summary: IN_QUEUE (with queue position) then IN_PROGRESS (with logs) then COMPLETED. Fal states requests are never dropped -- runners auto-scale to meet demand -- and failed requests auto-retry up to 10 times on 503/504/connection errors. A webhook_url at submit time replaces client polling. No documented latency figures. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai concurrency limit: new accounts get 2, scales to 40 as credits are purchased
summary: No requests-per-second limit is documented; fal instead caps concurrent in-flight requests per account. New accounts start at 2 concurrent requests; the limit auto-increases with credit purchases up to 40; higher needs sales contact. Requests over the limit queue rather than error. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai CDN output retention: two official docs pages disagree
summary: The FAQ page states generated media is available for at least 7 days by default. The dedicated media-expiration page instead lists Generated media (CDN files) retention as Configurable with no fixed default number, and its only worked example sets expiration_duration_seconds to 3600 (1 hour). Both pages read directly via raw fetch 2026-09-04; they do not agree, so treat 1 hour as the safe assumption and always set the header explicitly rather than relying on a default.

title: fal.ai media retention is per-request configurable via a header; expired files are unrecoverable
summary: X-Fal-Object-Lifecycle-Preference sets expiration_duration_seconds (or null for no expiration) on both uploaded inputs and generated outputs. fal states expired files are permanently deleted and cannot be recovered -- anything the site wants to keep long-term must be downloaded/copied (e.g. to R2) before it expires, not left on fal CDN. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai MCP (mcp.fal.ai/mcp) exposes 11 tools and authenticates with the raw API key on every request
summary: Discovery: search_models, get_model_schema, get_pricing, search_docs. Execution: run_model, submit_job, check_job, get_job_result, cancel_job. Utility: upload_file, recommend_model. Auth is an Authorization bearer header carrying the fal API key on every call; fal describes the hosted server as stateless with nothing stored server-side. Docs list only IDE/CLI clients (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) as supported clients, never a browser. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: a browser client can never safely use the fal MCP directly -- the key would have to sit in page JS
summary: fal MCP auth is a raw bearer token sent per request with no session, no scoping and no per-user limits (see the MCP tools/auth finding). A page cannot hold that token without exposing it to every viewer of that page (view-source, devtools network tab). This is the same reason Server/plugins/MCP.js -- the sites own MCP -- is loopback-only and never reachable from a browser. The MCP belongs in a coding agent talking to fal on the developers behalf, never in shipped site JS.

title: Cloudflare Workers AI: $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons, 10,000 Neurons/day free
summary: Confirmed on the official pricing page and cross-checked against an independent summary. Beyond the free 10k/day allocation a Workers Paid plan is required. 10k neurons roughly covers ~1,300 small LLM responses, ~12,500 embeddings, ~2,000 small (512x512) image generations, or ~8,300 image classifications per day, but the pool is shared across every model call that day. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: Cloudflare Workers AI Llama Guard 3 8B: about $0.48 per M input tokens, $0.03 per M output tokens
summary: Read twice: the platform pricing overview lists $0.484/M input + $0.030/M output (44,003 / 2,730 neurons per M tokens); the model-specific page rounds to $0.48/M input + $0.03/M output. At roughly 50 tokens per moderated message that is about 2.4 cents per 1,000 messages for input alone -- cheap enough to run synchronously on the message path. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: Cloudflare Workers AI text embeddings (BGE family): $0.020 to $0.204 per M input tokens by model size
summary: Smallest BGE embedding model: $0.020/M input tokens (1,841 neurons/M). Largest: $0.204/M input tokens (18,582 neurons/M). Topic titles for dedupe are a handful of tokens each, so embedding 10,000 topic titles (~100k tokens) costs about $0.002 on the small model -- inside the free daily neuron allowance even at meaningful topic-creation volume. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: OpenAI moderation endpoint (omni-moderation-latest) is free, text and image, not audio
summary: Confirmed directly on the official OpenAI docs: the moderation endpoint is free to use, image files up to 20MB. omni-moderation-latest classifies text and images in one request; some categories (harassment, hate, illicit activity) are text-only, others (sexual, violence, self-harm) apply to both text and images. No stated per-account rate limit in this doc; third-party summaries cite 250 RPM / 5,000 RPD for the free/default tier -- unverified against a primary rate-limits page. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: Google Perspective API is free but Google/Jigsaw is sunsetting it: service ends 2026-12-31
summary: Confirmed on the official perspectiveapi.com FAQ, fetched directly: the service remains active until December 31, 2026; usage and quota-increase requests are addressed only until February 2026; no direct migration support is offered. Perspective API is therefore not a safe moderation dependency for a platform launching around now -- it would need replacing within its first year. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: Perspective API default quota: about 1 query per second per project
summary: From search-aggregated summaries of developers.perspectiveapi.com (a Salesforce-hosted JS page that returns no static text to a direct fetch, so this could not be independently re-confirmed by reading the raw page a second time). Stated as enough for testing/dev, not production volume, and moot regardless given the 2026-12-31 sunset. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai applies its own content filters; a flagged request fails with a non-retryable 422
summary: The FAQ states fal applies content filters on certain models: a request flagged by automated safety systems returns a content_policy_violation error, documented as a non-retryable 422 (unlike 503/504 which auto-retry). This is a free, automatic first line of image moderation on anything generated through fal, independent of any moderation the site adds itself. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small: $0.02 per M tokens, same order as Workers AI cheapest embedding
summary: text-embedding-3-small costs $0.02/M tokens via the standard API (a Batch API discount brings it to $0.01/M for non-urgent jobs). This lands within a few percent of Cloudflare Workers AI bge-small at $0.020/M input tokens -- for pure per-token cost the two are a wash; the real difference is one more vendor key vs reusing infrastructure already needed for other Workers AI calls. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: Correction/confirm: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small $0.02/M tokens, verified on developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing
summary: The earlier entry cited openai.com/api/pricing/, which returns HTTP 403 to a direct fetch and was only checked via search-engine summaries. Re-verified by fetching the redirect target directly: text-embedding-3-small is $0.02 per 1M tokens, text-embedding-3-large is $0.13 per 1M tokens. Use this url, not the 403ing one, as the citation. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: Claude API current pricing: Sonnet 5 $2/$10 per M tokens in/out, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5
summary: From Anthropic first-party API pricing (also what Server/plugins/Ask.js pays for a turn today). Sonnet 5: $2.00 input / $10.00 output per M tokens. Haiku 4.5: $1.00 / $5.00 per M tokens, 200K context. These are the two candidates for AI-drafted topic pages -- Sonnet for outline quality, Haiku for the cheap duplicate/summary path. Checked 2026-09-04 against the bundled claude-api skill reference.

title: estimated cost per AI-drafted topic page: about 2-5 cents on Sonnet, under 2 cents on Haiku
summary: Not measured against a real prompt -- a rough estimate from Claude API per-token pricing assuming an outline + 10-minute-intro brief + subtopic map runs about 2k input / 3k output tokens. Sonnet 5: (2000/1e6*2)+(3000/1e6*10) = ~$0.034/draft. Haiku 4.5: ~$0.017/draft but likely needs a human edit pass regardless. Treat as a ballpark until someone runs it for real and logs response.usage.

title: fal.ai does not host LLMs -- fal-ai/any-llm proxies to OpenRouter for 200+ text models
summary: fals own tutorial documents the any-llm endpoint as a single API surface over Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen, Mistral and more, powered by OpenRouter under the hood. So calling Claude through fal means going through two paid middlemen (fal, then OpenRouter) instead of the Anthropic API directly. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: call Anthropic directly for topic/content generation; keep fal scoped to image, video, audio and 3D only
summary: Given fal-ai/any-llm is an OpenRouter proxy (extra hop, extra markup, no model fal does not already expose indirectly) and the site already has Server/plugins/Ask.js talking to Claude directly, there is no reason to route text generation through fal. One fewer vendor in the trust chain for the highest-stakes AI feature (wiki-shaped topic text).

title: Correction: Claude pricing url is claude.com/pricing, not developers.anthropic.com/docs/pricing
summary: The earlier Claude Sonnet 5 / Haiku 4.5 pricing entry cited a url that was never independently fetched. Re-verified by fetching claude.com/pricing directly: Sonnet 5 $2/MTok in, $10/MTok out; Haiku 4.5 $1/MTok in, $5/MTok out; both get a 50 percent batch-API discount. Numbers match the earlier entry -- only the citation url was wrong. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai 3D generation: Hunyuan3D v2 image-to-3D, $0.16/generation (white mesh), $0.48 with textures
summary: Confirmed via direct fetch of the model page. Newer v3.1 tiers: Rapid $0.225/generation, Pro $0.375 (+$0.15 for PBR materials, +$0.15 for multi-view input). All marked commercial-use licensed on fals own catalog. This is the family for the WebGL/3D idea in the brief. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai speech-to-text (Wizper/Whisper v3): roughly $0.0008/second (~$0.05/minute), not independently re-confirmed
summary: Search-aggregated figure; fals own Wizper model page renders its price through a client-side JS calculator that shows a placeholder $0 to a static fetch and could not be read a second, independent way. Treat this number as a starting estimate for transcript-driven content assistance (chapters/summaries from video), not a locked-in figure -- verify against a real fal invoice before using it in a cost table that matters.

title: fal.ai Flux Kontext Pro (image editing/variation): $0.04/image
summary: An image-to-image editing model, not text-to-image from scratch -- takes an existing image plus an instruction and returns a variation. Directly relevant to the brief instruction that AI should vary the owners existing badge designs, not originate new ones. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: badges: drive Flux Kontext (image-to-image) from the owners existing art, never a from-scratch generator
summary: Matches the briefs own instruction (AI as variation, not origin). Feed the owners badge source art into Flux Kontext Pro ($0.04/image) or a cheaper img2img model for style variants (bronze/silver/gold tiers, seasonal skins), with a human approving before anything ships. Never let a user prompt a badge into existence unsupervised.

title: fal.ai output ownership: the licensor claims no rights in generated output; commercial use is per-model
summary: fals FAQ states the licensor (fal/the underlying model provider) claims no rights in output, and the user is accountable for that outputs subsequent use. Most models carry a Commercial use badge on their model page, but this is model-by-model, not blanket -- check every model actually used, not just the family.

title: Black Forest Labs FLUX.1 dev weights are non-commercial-only under the raw open license; schnell is Apache 2.0
summary: The LICENSE-FLUX1-dev file on Black Forest Labs GitHub restricts Non-Commercial Purpose use only (personal research, hobby, or paid-entity testing/evaluation with no payment received) and explicitly excludes production/commercial use. FLUX.1 schnell instead ships under Apache 2.0, fully commercial-friendly. This is the license for the raw weights, not necessarily for a hosted API call -- see the contested entry on fals own dev-model page. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai own flux/dev model page contradicts the raw Black Forest Labs dev license: labels itself commercial
summary: fal.ai/models/fal-ai/flux/dev states the model is suitable for personal and commercial use and its own metadata sets licenseType: commercial -- read directly from the pages raw HTML. This is inconsistent with Black Forest Labs own non-commercial-only LICENSE-FLUX1-dev for the raw weights (separate entry). Most likely fal has a separate commercial hosting agreement with BFL that only covers calls made through fals API, but that is inferred, not documented anywhere fal-side -- worth a direct question to fal support before shipping commercial output from flux/dev specifically (schnell and the pro API tier avoid the question entirely). Checked 2026-09-04.

title: Cloudflare Worker secrets are write-only: encrypted at rest, never readable back once set
summary: Confirmed on the official Workers secrets docs and a security-focused third-party writeup: env vars/secrets are injected into a Workers memory at boot, encrypted at rest, and cannot be retrieved via API or dashboard after creation -- only rotated. Cloudflare Secrets Store additionally centralizes account-level secrets shared across multiple Workers. This is where the FAL_KEY belongs; never in a KV value, never in a response body. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: the safe /api/generate shape: Worker-held key, signed short-lived job token, per-user/day cap, proxy-only response
summary: Standard Workers-as-proxy pattern: (1) FAL_KEY lives only in a Worker secret, never sent to the browser; (2) the browser calls a same-origin /api/generate under its own session auth, not the fal key; (3) the Worker checks a per-user-per-day counter (Durable Object or KV) before calling fal, so nothing can spend the account dry; (4) the Worker calls fal server-side and returns only the resulting CDN url, never a fal-issued bearer; (5) submit-then-poll for anything slower than a couple seconds so the Worker is not held open by fals queue. This is the generic secret-proxy pattern applied to fal -- no source models it for fal specifically.

title: what are the actual per-user-per-day dollar caps and abuse gates for /api/generate?
summary: Neither fal nor Cloudflare picks this number for you -- it is a product decision, not a vendor fact. A public image generator with no cap is, as the brief itself says, a free GPU for the internet. Needs: a dollar ceiling per user per day, a lower ceiling (or a Turnstile challenge) for anonymous/unauthenticated callers, and a kill switch if the daily fal bill spikes. Nobody has picked numbers yet -- the most useful open item in this log.

title: Cloudflare Workers AI has no dedicated image-safety/NSFW classifier in its model catalog
summary: Workers AI ships Llama Guard 3 for text safety classification and general-purpose image classification (e.g. resnet-50 for object labels), but no image moderation/NSFW-specific model. For image moderation the two free options are fals own automatic content_policy_violation filter (generation-time only) and OpenAI omni-moderation-latest (free, accepts image input, works on anything generated or user-uploaded). Checked 2026-09-04.

title: moderation first line: fal automatic filter + OpenAI omni-moderation, both free, both async where possible
summary: Recommend fals own content_policy_violation filter (free, runs at generation time, no extra call) as line one for AI-generated images, plus OpenAI omni-moderation-latest (free, text+image, no known rate limit documented) as line two on the message/post path, run async after the post is accepted rather than blocking on it. Llama Guard 3 stays the fallback for text if OpenAIs free tier ever becomes a bottleneck (about 2.4 cents/1k messages). This is a recommendation, not a settled architecture -- false-positive handling and what must stay human are still open (see the challenge question on AI moderation as first line).

title: AI moderation as the first line vs the last: what stays human, and what is the false-positive appeal path?
summary: The brief itself asks this as a challenge. No vendor doc answers it -- Llama Guard, OpenAI moderation and fals filter all classify, none of them adjudicate. A wrongly-blocked post needs a visible appeal path, and permanent bans/removals (the highest-stakes actions) should never be a bare model score with no human in the loop. This needs its own decision record, not a vendor citation -- flagging it as unresolved rather than inventing an answer.

title: AI-drafted wiki text: plagiarism and hallucination risk is real and nobody sells a guarantee against it
summary: No vendor (Anthropic, fal, OpenAI) offers an accuracy or originality guarantee on generated text -- this is well-known LLM behavior, not a specific finding from any doc read this session. An AI-drafted topic outline can fabricate facts, phrase existing sources too closely, or misattribute. The only mitigation found in any doc is human review before publish (the briefs own human-in-the-loop gate). Open: does the MVP publish any AI-drafted wiki text without an editor click-through? Recommend: no.

title: fal.ai video pricing: Wan 2.5 $0.05/sec, Kling 2.5 Turbo Pro $0.07/sec, Veo 3 $0.40/sec
summary: From fals own pricing page. Video is priced per output second, not per generation, so an 8-second clip on the cheapest of these three runs about $0.40, and about $3.20 on Veo 3. No fal video model appears in the closed question list as load-bearing for the MVP -- topic art and badges are images/3D, not video -- so this is catalogue completeness, not a recommendation. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: fal.ai free-tier utility tools (background remover, upscaler) show $0 on their own pricing calculator, unclear if truly free
summary: The main fal.ai/pricing page lists Background Remover, Image Upscaler, Image Extender and Image Resizer under a Free/Utility Tools heading. But the individual model pages (e.g. birefnet background removal) render pricing through a client-side calculator that defaults to $0 per compute second before any input is given -- the same placeholder pattern seen on Wizper speech-to-text. Could not confirm a nonzero per-call rate exists behind that calculator. Treat as free until proven otherwise, not confirmed free. Checked 2026-09-04.

title: third-party aggregators claim fal.ai runs 30-50pct cheaper than Replicate with a larger model catalog
summary: Practitioner/aggregator blog claims (pricepertoken.com, teamday.ai, workflowlab.dev), not confirmed against Replicates own pricing page in this session. They agree fal and Replicate charge the same $0.003/image for Flux Schnell, and that fal has faster cold starts (single-digit seconds vs Replicates 10-120s) via a warm pool. Argued by sources that name their numbers, but not cross-checked against Replicate directly -- fringe until read against a primary Replicate source.

title: challenge: is fal.ai the right primary provider vs Workers AI, Replicate, or direct model APIs? -- yes, for image/video/3D/audio only
summary: fal wins on catalog breadth (600+ models incl. FLUX/Hunyuan3D/Wan/Wizper) and a queue API built for slow jobs -- Workers AI has none of image-gen-family/3D/serious video. Workers AI wins on billing simplicity (one Cloudflare bill, free daily allowance) for the small stuff: text moderation (Llama Guard), embeddings, light image classification. Direct model APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI) win for anything text/LLM-shaped -- fals any-llm is a needless OpenRouter hop. Recommendation: fal for image/video/3D/audio only; Workers AI for embeddings + text moderation; Anthropic direct for topic/content text. Contested -- nobody has run a real invoice through either provider yet.

title: challenge: is any AI needed in the MVP at all? -- no, AI is entirely deferable to post-MVP
summary: Every AI feature in this brief (topic drafting, dedupe embeddings, content assistance, moderation beyond a manual report button, image/badge/3D generation) sits after step 10 in the briefs own MVP philosophy (section 31), behind users/auth/permissions/community. A static topic page a human writes, plus a manual report-and-review moderation queue, ships a working MVP with zero AI vendor risk, zero key-handling surface, and zero recurring AI bill. AI is the first thing to cut if the MVP must shrink.

title: topic-creation cost table at 1k users/month, light-activity mix
summary: Rough estimate, not measured: 1,000 users, 20 new topics/month (Sonnet 5 draft ~$0.03 each = $0.60), 20 topic-art images on flux/schnell ($0.003 each = $0.06), 200 dedupe-embedding checks on Workers AI bge-small (near-zero, inside free tier), 5,000 posts/month through OpenAI free moderation ($0) plus Llama Guard spot-checks on ~500 flagged posts (~25k tokens, about $0.01). Total under $1/month in raw AI spend at this scale -- abuse, not legitimate use, is the real cost driver, which is why the per-user cap matters more than the per-call price.

title: skeptic pass: "call Anthropic directly" is a judgment call, not an established fact -- downgrading from the earlier established tag
summary: The earlier entry recommending Anthropic-direct over fal any-llm graded itself established, but this is architectural taste, not vendor consensus -- a counter-argument exists (one billing relationship, one key to rotate, if fal is already the only AI vendor in the stack). The technical facts underneath (any-llm proxies through OpenRouter, extra hop) are established; the recommendation built on them is contested. Logging this correction rather than editing the original entry.

title: skeptic pass: the badges-use-Flux-Kontext recommendation is one plausible tool choice, not the only one -- downgrading from established
summary: The earlier badges entry graded itself established, but Flux Kontext is one of several img2img/editing models on fal (Flux Redux, Qwen image-edit variants also exist per fals own catalog groupings) and none were compared head to head on quality for this specific use case (variations on existing badge line art). The instruction to vary rather than originate is established (its the briefs own words); the specific model pick is a starting guess.

title: skeptic pass: could a scoped, short-lived fal token ever make MCP-from-browser safe? -- not with what fal documents today
summary: The MCP-never-browser opinion rests on fal MCP auth being the raw account key with no scoping. Checked fal MCP docs for a token-exchange or scoped-credential mechanism (the kind Anthropics own OAuth short-lived access tokens provide) and found none documented -- every request just carries Authorization: Bearer <your fal API key>. If fal ever ships scoped tokens for MCP specifically, this verdict would need revisiting; today it holds. Not fully closed since fal could add this at any time without it showing in general docs search.

title: skeptic pass: the fal-vs-Workers-AI split leans on one uncross-checked claim (the fringe Replicate comparison) for cost framing
summary: The primary-provider opinion cites fal catalog breadth and Workers AI billing simplicity, both independently established elsewhere in this log, so the recommendation itself does not actually depend on the fringe Replicate-comparison entry -- checked, and it holds without it. Flagging this cross-reference explicitly so a reader does not assume the fringe entry is load-bearing for the primary recommendation.
